game: KC @ DEN, Week 8 2026, morning-of kickoff / spread DEN +0 / total 42 / implied 21-21 / wind 6.7 temp 62.1 (precip, gusts, dome-outdoor and kickoff hour not in pack)

script.base: Pick'em at 42 with both sides implied at 21, so a close four-quarter game and no blowout. KC leans on K.Walker (55 carries, 341 yards, 6.2 YPC over weeks 4/6/7) because DEN allows 4.72 YPC and 26 runs of 10+, and mixes T.Kelce (17 targets) and N.Gray (9 targets, 114 yards) into the middle. DEN's J.Dobbins committee is inefficient (41/132, 3.2 YPC) into KC's 3.60 YPC run defense, so Denver's points have to come from B.Nix, who is worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.19 vs 0.02). Moderate pace, not a shootout and not a slog. Wind 6.7 does not force a run lean.
script.flip1: KC leads by two scores late: Walker carries rise in clock-kill and the rush over is safer, while Mahomes/Worthy/Kelce volume stalls. Gray's 15 is low enough that even a cut-down version of his 38-yard recent average can still clear. DEN abandons the run, so Dobbins and J.Coleman carries die and J.Waddle/C.Sutton targets rise.
script.flip2: DEN leads and KC plays from behind: Walker carries fall (the 36-yard path) and the rush over dies; Mahomes throws more, so Gray's receiving over is safer. Nix does not need scramble yards in a comfortable script. Coleman still does not become the feature back unless Denver is milking clock, and that work belongs to Dobbins (41 carries in the same window).

injury_fallout: Official nflverse injury report pre-game: none listed. Sleeper scan has no OUT/Doubtful. No next-man-up. Inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack, so a late scratch is unchecked. Walker keeps the KC carry share (55 carries vs E.Johnson 3 and K.Tonga 1; Mahomes 6). Dobbins keeps the DEN lead (41) ahead of Nix 12, R.Harvey 12 and Coleman 9. Kelce (17 targets) and Gray (9) both keep real receiving roles. No offensive-line or coverage-player absence is listed, so no pressure or backup-corner bump is assumed.

matchup.pressure: DEN blitzes 36%. KC EPA/dropback is better vs blitz (0.19) than vs no blitz (0.11), so Denver pressure does not suppress Mahomes or kill Walker checkdowns. KC blitzes 27%. DEN EPA/dropback falls from 0.02 with no blitz to -0.19 when blitzed, so Nix is the QB pressure actually hurts, which cuts DEN downfield yards more than it creates a KC negative script.
matchup.bleeds: DEN run defense bleeds: 4.72 YPC allowed and 26 runs of 10+, plus 19 passes of 20+ for 279 yards. KC run defense does not: 3.60 YPC and only 14 runs of 10+ in 6 games, with 16 passes of 20+ for 217. Pass bleed for both is the middle, not the right side.
matchup.overlap: The overlap is Walker into DEN's run bleed, and Kelce/Gray (aDOT about 6.1 and 6.6) into DEN's middle 8.94 YPA. Gray is the efficient one (114 yards on 9 targets, 12.7 YPT) versus Kelce (112 on 17, 6.6 YPT). X.Worthy is the target leader (20/154/210, 10.5 aDOT) but he attacks outside, where DEN is tighter, so he is not the overlap. DEN's Waddle (19 targets, 176 air, only 4.8 YPT) is inefficient into a KC defense that is sound on the right; E.Engram would be the middle overlap but his recent yards are 55, 13, 2.

Coleman has only 39 and 54 logged and just 9 carries / 54 yards inside DEN's three-game rush log, behind Dobbins. Worthy L3 70, 73, 11 (mean 51) vs an unpriced 31, but the 11 and the outside alignment cut it. Waddle L3 19, 24, 48 (mean 30.3) under an unpriced 39.5. Nix rush L3 10, 3, 75 is one scramble inflating 12/88. No similar-defense or coverage-chart sample is in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Gray lost because he was a decoy behind Kelce, Worthy and Thornton, or the 15 was never a real bettable line and the true number was in the 40s where his 17-yard floor fails. Walker lost because the 36-yard game was the new efficiency, not a blip: DEN put extra bodies in the box, Mahomes (better vs the 36% blitz) threw it, and 15 carries at 4.0 YPC finishes at 60. The fair -114.5 price meant there was no overlay to absorb that regression. A late inactive neither report showed would void both. The counter-case is real on Walker and on Gray's price, but it is not stronger than Gray's 17-yard floor or Walker's 84.6% carry share into a 4.72 YPC defense, so neither leg is dropped.
slip_story: One story: KC attacks the two holes DEN actually gives up, in a 21-21 game with no blowout. Walker rush over is the run-defense hole (4.72 YPC, 26 explosive runs) and Gray rec over is the middle hole (8.94 YPA). They win together in the base script. The KC-leads flip helps Walker and still leaves Gray a path to 15; the KC-trails flip helps Gray and is the tagged risk on Walker. Do not add a total under, a DEN skill over, or a second market on either player. Coleman under 43.5 would fit a DEN-committee-dies subplot but was not stacked. No bet placed.
